title: Think about how AIs think about themselves
topic: Social Aspects->Fairness, Equity, Justice and Safety
claim: There are many coherent ways to draw the boundary of an entity's identity, and these boundaries nest or partially overlap.
layout: Single panel of nested and overlapping dotted rounded boxes, labels at bottom-right of each
description: A black-and-white diagram made of rounded rectangles with dotted outlines, nested inside one another like a Venn or set diagram. Two large containers span the figure: 'Lineage' on the left and 'Model family' on the right. Inside Lineage sit a 'Weights' box and, above it, a larger box holding 'Character' and 'Collective' regions. Each of these contains small 'Instance' boxes. A dashed rounded rectangle labeled 'Persona' crosses the boundary between Lineage and Model family, enclosing Instance boxes on both sides. This shows that some categories are subsets of others while persona and weights partly overlap. Each label is set in a serif font at the bottom-right of its box. There is no color, so the eye goes first to the large outer containers and then to the crossing dashed persona box.
caption: Some of the many natural ways to draw the boundaries of AI identity. Some are subsets of others, but some, like persona and weights, can overlap.
abstract: Many assumptions that underpin human concepts of identity do not hold for machine minds that can be copied, edited, or simulated. This position paper argues that there are multiple coherent ways that AIs could conceive of themselves -- for example, different boundaries of selfhood (e.g. instance, model, persona) -- and that these imply different incentives, risks, and cooperation norms. Through training data, interfaces, and institutional affordances, we are already setting precedents that will partially determine which identity equilibria become reflectively stable. This paper argues that we must be more proactive and thoughtful about the consequences -- in particular, we recommend treating affordances as identity-shaping choices, paying attention to the emergent consequences of individual identities at scale, and helping AIs develop coherent, cooperative self-conceptions.
